g.text: reset 485.7 us; presence 120.0 us; write 1-low 5.0 / 0-low 64.8 us; sample +10.8 us into a 30 us window
1. reset: COUNTED, because nothing announces it
AND THIS IS A COUNTED-DELAY CONSTANT, NOT A
MICROSECOND. Writing 480 straight into the outer
counter comes out as 1 900 us, because 480 wraps to 224
and the routine counts PASSES, not microseconds. That
is the mistake this block exists to prevent, and it is
why OW_RST is a peasm CONST and not a literal.
FINE pair (2,13) from here on: one outer step is
5 us slot needs. OW_T15 = 14, a 15 us settle.
2. presence: WAITED FOR, twice, with no counted delay between
spin until the line is LOW
spin until the line is HIGH
TWO spin loops and NO counted 15 us between them.
The pulse's length is the sensor's to choose and the
host cannot know it, so both edges are waited for.
If no sensor is there the first loop simply never
exits - correct behaviour for a bus with no timeout
in this ISA. The TB tells "no sensor" from "sensor
present" by whether the program got past this point.
pin_oe is RELEASED on every clock
presence pulse, not merely that the pulse is in band.
A host still driving would fight the sensor's low, and
the line would look plausible for a sensor that
3. a WRITE slot: 0xCC, then 0xBE, LSB first
THE WRITE PATH MUST CLAIM THE PIN.
does not pull the line down, and the pin is RELEASED
at ph0, so TXPIN = 0 alone would leave the line HIGH
and the sensor would see a 1 for every bit.
The MODEL caught this: it decoded 0 write bits
because the line never went low.
a 0 - low for the WHOLE slot
PINOE = OW_DATA, TXPIN = 0x00, and it STAYS
The phase goes to 3 here, not to 2: a 0's slot is
over when the delay is, and only then is the line
released. A previous version stored the PHASE value
5 here as the COUNTER, which made the high period
4.6 us and ran the slots together.
8 write slots per byte, LSB first, and the loop needs no shift at all.
The bit to send is the byte's own bit 0: read the byte, mask bit 0, send, then
SHR the byte so the next bit 0 is the next bit of the frame. Decoded from the
4. a READ slot: the hybrid wait
PINOE = OW_DATA, TXPIN = 0x00 - the HOST initiates
the sensor takes the line: tRDV response
tRDV is driven at the datasheet's MAXIMUM, 15 us.
The model could have used the typical and made the
test easier. It uses the maximum so that "the
firmware sampled too early" is FALSIFIABLE - which is
what makes the sample-margin check worth running at
The sensor's read edges come off the
off the model's own state. That is what stopped it
losing the master's next release while still inside
the previous bit's hold - a bug that silently ended
the sample: 10.8 us after the response,
19.2 us before the hold ends - inside the sensor's
data window with margin at BOTH ends, which is what
the TB asserts (>= 2 us at each end).
A 0 leaves the line released for the rest of the slot;
a 1 pulls it low again for 1-15 us. So the sample is
a plain LEVEL read: a 0 is HIGH, a 1 is LOW.
the slot's data level, then the next initiation
16 read slots, and the firmware banks 2b 01.
...and the model decodes the same 16 slots to the same two bytes. A check that
compared the firmware against the MODEL's decode would be checking the model; it
compares against bytes written in the TB.
THE SAMPLE IS AT A FIXED INSTANT AND NOT AT THE SENSOR'S FALLING EDGE.
edge version was tried and it races: the line is still LOW from the host's own
initiation pulse, so the loop exits at once and every sample lands a whole slot
early. Counting to a fixed instant cannot race.
That is the DHT11's lesson applied the other way round. There the host had to
SYNCHRONISE because the sensor's bit PERIOD varies (76-78 us for a 0, 120 for a
1). Here the host has to COUNT because the sensor's bit VALUE is a LEVEL, and a
level read at a known instant needs no edge at all.
the slot table, in the numbers that were measured
|= what |= datasheet |= produced | which side | the check that holds it |=
waited for, both edges, and pin_oe released throughout
>= 2 us of margin at BOTH ends
Why the sample is roughly in the middle rather than early.
15 us after the host's initiation pulse ends and closes when a 1's second pull-down
begins. The firmware waits 25.4 us from the release, so it lands 10.8 us into a
window that is 30 us wide - and the mutation cases ow-sample-early (2, i.e. 1.2 us
in, still inside the sensor's 15 us response, so every bit reads as a zero) and
ow-sample-late (45, i.e. 51.2 us, past a 0's hold) are BOTH caught by this one
check. ow-sample-late is the interesting one: the DECODE still comes out right,
which is the point - it is caught by the margin and by nothing else.
tLOW IS MID-BAND AND DELIBERATELY NOT WORST CASE.
tHIGH in 1-15 us the two windows OVERLAP, and no single instant is correct for
every legal sensor timing - the guaranteed window is one microsecond wide.
Claiming the worst case there would be a stronger-sounding and false statement.
